lyrics: Fifteen years old,
punching clocks, learned the meaning of a buck.
Fifteen years old,
punching clocks, learned the meaning of a buck.
Military discipline
made me strong,   through every bit of
luck. GI Bill in one hand,
graveyard shifts in the   other, pushing through the
muck.         Now I'm in my sweet
repose, earned   beneath the
country sky.   Every lesson, every
struggle,     whispered by the years
gone by. Got   my hands in
honest dirt,   my own hard
path I've tried.   The self-made man's
repose, a     quiet blessing plain to
see.
Burned the midnight oil
then worked the day,   pushed myself 'til I felt
raw. Burned the midnight oil
then worked the day,   pushed myself 'til I felt
raw. Thirty-five   years in the
digital hum,   living by a
different law. Building systems, climbing
high, 'til retirement,   answered nature's
call.         Now I'm in my sweet
repose, earned beneath the
country sky.   Every lesson, every
struggle,     whispered by the years
gone by. Got   my hands in
honest dirt, my own hard
path I've tried.   The self-made man's
repose, a     quiet blessing plain to
see. Now I walk these fields
at dawn,      where the green things
gently grow. Now I walk these fields
at dawn, where   the green things
gently grow. No   more city's frantic
pace, just    the river's steady
flow. And the peace I built for
myself, every seed   that I now sow.
The           body knows the years
it's seen, every   scar, every ache and
pain. But the   spirit's strong, the mind is
keen, through   sunshine and the gentle
rain. From    a young man's drive to
an old man's calm,   a journey
long and true.   This quiet life, this
tranquil farm,   is everything I dreamed
it through.
